prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Move sign-in after pet adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured +5.1% ± 2.1%, after noise correction +3.5%, won
- round 1: Waiting step progress timer & delay callout [home, wait_info]: predicted +6.0%, measured +2.9% ± 2.6%, after noise correction +1.7%, lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Clear onboarding intro story narrative [choose_path, copy]: predicted +2.0%, measured -3.9% ± 1.4%, after noise correction -3.3%, lost: worse
- round 2: Ready notification toggle on wait screen [home, notification]: predicted +2.0%, measured +3.8% ± 2.1%, after noise correction +2.7%, lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Two-column desktop command layout [finish, layout]: predicted +3.0%, measured -3.2% ± 3.4%, after noise correction -1.5%, lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Redesign friend selection to grid with live preview [adoption, redesign]: predicted +15.0%, measured +12.1% ± 2.8%, after noise correction +6.8%, won, confirmed by re-test

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- adoption, redesign: +6.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, copy: -3.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, layout: -1.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, notification: +2.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: +1.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Previous lessons:
Evidence is still thin for specific change types, as only one test has been run so far for both sign-in reordering (sign_in, reorder) and waiting step callouts (home, wait_info).
Predictions were consistently too high compared to noise-corrected measured outcomes.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Evidence is still thin for specific change types because no change type has at least two tests agreeing after noise correction.
Redesigning friend selection (adoption, redesign) and moving sign-in (sign_in, reorder) were helpful, winning their tests.
Updating onboarding intro story copy (choose_path, copy) made performance worse.
No clear effect was seen for waiting step info (home, wait_info), notification toggles (home, notification), or layout changes (finish, layout).
Predictions were consistently too high compared to noise-corrected measured outcomes.
